newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria has $15.3 mln first half c/a surplus.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria has $15.3 mln first half c/a surplus.

text.p: Bulgaria posted a current account surplus of $15.3 million in the first half of this year after a $106.7 million deficit in the same period of 1995, preliminary Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) customs-based figures show.
BULGARIA CURRENT A/C, MLN USD H1 H1'95
current account +15.3 -106.7
trade balance +155.8 +40.2
exports FOB 2,143.1 2,521.2
imports FOB 1,987.3 2,481.0
services net +14.2 +16.3
receipts 573.9 639.4
payments 559.7 623.1
capital account -71.9 -22.3

Based on preliminary customs figures Bulgaria's trade balance for the first six months posted a surplus of $155.8 million but according to data from commercial banks Bulgaria faced a trade deficit of $172.2 million, BNB statistics showed.
Banks reported $2,734.7 million exports FOB and $2,907.0 million imports FOB in the first half of 1996.

The discrepancy, which could be explained with delays in processing customs data could however indicate a large outflow of capital masked by fictitious imports of goods and services, a financial analyst who declined to be named told Reuters.

The depreciation of the Bulgarian lev against major currencies in the first six months was beneficial for the country's exports but the fall in the growth rate in the member countries of the European Union led to lower demand for imports there, including ones from Bulgaria, the BNB said.
According to BNB data Bulgaria's exports to those countries accounted for 40.2 percent of total exports during the period.
The lev declined to 156 per dollar at the end of June, from around 71 at the beginning of 1996.

Record high interest rates on credits to non-financial institutions of around 120 percent annually at the end of June, additionally curtailed production and exports of goods and services, the central bank said.
State industrial production fell by a real 4.0 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1996, National Statistics Institute figures showed.

Revenue from interest payments on credits extended by the country totalled $58.0 million, while interest payments to foreign creditors of the government and commercial banks ammounted to $288.8 million, BNB data showed.
-- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
